svg.text: Priority operations II: fold, extrude, skim, baste, deglaze, proof
Six cook’s operations made explicit with existing hardware plus one blade, one tube, a ladle and a few rules.
G-assembly-meat · section 6 (6.4, 6.5, 6.10–6.12, 6.14)
mostly conf. H
Spätzle and mousse have no fallback
rub-in, cream, sift: existing blade / beater / whisk
GA-32 Fold: fixed blade, turning bowl
FLD, 11 meals · volume loss ≤ 20 %
Spätzle: piston tube with hole plate
EXT, 3 meals (8 weight points), no fallback
Skim: weir ladle
SKM · first choice: blanch and rinse the meat
Baste: tilt the tin, spoon the jus
BST, 9 meals · or self-basting by design
Deglaze: rules against spatter
DGL, 24 meals
Rest, proof: watch the dome
RES, PRF, 11 meals

g.text: 1/6 Fold: the bowl turns under a fixed blade set at 45°, which lifts the bottom and lays it over — the hand fold, moved into the bowl.
2/6 Spätzle: a piston presses batter through 2.5–3 mm holes straight into the simmering pot.
3/6 Skim: a ladle is held level just under the surface; only the fat layer runs over its rim.
4/6 Baste: the tin is tilted 5° so the jus pools in a known corner, then spooned over.
5/6 Deglaze: liquid first slowly at the wall inside a splash ring, then the fond is scraped free.
6/6 Proof: the dough rises in a straight-walled lidded bowl; the dome height says when it has doubled.
